title: Inside the Codex sandbox
headline: OpenAI details sandbox security architecture for Codex agentic harness
summary: OpenAI has published technical details regarding the Codex sandbox, a security feature designed to restrict the filesystem and network access of AI agents. The system uses OS-specific mechanisms—Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap and seccomp-bpf on Linux, and native Windows facilities—to enforce permission profiles. These profiles allow administrators and users to define granular constraints on agent behaviour, such as read-only access or network blocking, to mitigate risks like data exfiltration or malicious code injection.
why_it_matters: Organisations deploying AI agents can use these sandboxing techniques to implement a defense-in-depth strategy, ensuring that agentic tools operate within defined security boundaries that prevent unauthorised system access.

quotes.text: we built the Codex sandbox so Codex can work in your existing environment within filesystem and network limits you control.
This is why we take a defense in depth approach: the sandbox limits what commands can access, while training and alignment help the model use that access in accordance with the user’s intent.
Administrators can also supply managed requirements ⁠ (opens in a new window) through requirements.toml to constrain users’ configuration choices.

classification.significance_reason: Provides a technical blueprint for implementing security controls in agentic AI systems, which is a critical area for enterprise risk management.
